problem_text:
A logistics firm must dispatch a maintenance crew to inspect five critical substations across a region.  
The substations are positioned at the following grid coordinates (in kilometers):  
Station Alpha: (193, 33)  
Station Beta: (38, 9)  
Station Gamma: (20, 179)  
Station Delta: (138, 174)  
Station Epsilon: (100, 180)  

Travel distances between substations are known precisely:  
Alpha to Gamma: 226.4 km  
Alpha to Delta: 151.3 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 173.9 km  
Beta to Gamma: 171.0 km  
Beta to Delta: 192.9 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 181.9 km  
Gamma to Delta: 118.1 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 80.0 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 38.5 km  

Due to terrain restrictions, there is no direct access route linking Alpha and Beta.  
Furthermore, operational regulations mandate that exactly one of the following two connections must be part of the inspection circuit: the link between Beta and Gamma, or the link between Gamma and Delta.  

The objective is to determine the most efficient closed-loop itinerary that visits every substation exactly once and returns to the origin point, minimizing the total travel distance.
